top_jobs.job: When I am working 70 hour weeks and still the bottleneck on every decision, help me see which work others can own and who should own it, so I get 10 hours back for the calls only I can make
top_jobs.metric: decisions waiting on the founder over 48 hours, weekly

top_jobs.job: When a key person gives notice or I want 2 weeks off, help me see what only one person knows and holds, logins, contacts and steps, so the business does not stop when someone leaves
top_jobs.metric: critical logins, contacts and tasks only one person can do, quarterly

top_jobs.job: When the warehouse, the factory, the agency or a software vendor does not deliver what we pay for, help me hold them to the contract with dates and numbers, so I get credits and fix the service
top_jobs.metric: vendor misses against the contract, and credits claimed, monthly

top_jobs.job: When the team says it is drowning or a peak is coming, help me see the load per person from tickets, tasks and orders, so I shift work or hire on numbers, not feelings
top_jobs.metric: workload per person against the written hiring trigger, monthly

top_jobs.job: When work sits across people, screens and vendors, help me see every task, owner and date on one board, so nothing is found missing the week before a launch

jobs.job: Put every open task from every screen, Slack thread and the founder's notes on one kanban board with 5 columns (to do, doing, waiting on approval, live, measured), each card with 1 owner, a due date and the metric it should move
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then every task any screen or person creates lands on it

inputs.need: tasks proposed by each screen and agent
team list with roles and weekly hours
approval rules: who approves what and spend caps
a board tool if we do not host one yet (Trello, Notion or a Google Sheet)

steps: Pull open tasks from the founder's inbox, Slack and last 2 meeting notes into one list
Merge duplicates and drop anything nobody will do in the next 60 days
Give each card 1 owner, a due date and the metric it should move
Place each card in one of the 5 columns
Founder checks the waiting on approval column and clears or rejects each card
Set a rule: no card moves to live without a metric, and none to measured without a before and after number
jobs.output: a board with every open task, 1 owner and 1 due date each, and a count of cards with no owner (target 0)
jobs.next: feeds 23-04 (launch plan), 23-05 (load per person) and 26-03 (what shipped and what it did)

watch.metric: share of open tasks with 1 owner and a due date

jobs.drives: tasks late against plan, and decisions waiting on the founder

jobs.job: List every recurring task the founder did in the last 2 weeks from the calendar, inbox and board, and mark each one keep, hand off or drop, with a named owner and a check for each hand off
jobs.trigger: once, then every quarter and whenever the founder's week runs over 60 hours

inputs.need: the founder's calendar and sent mail for the last 14 days
team list with skills and spare hours
open and done cards per person
what only the founder may decide

steps: Pull every meeting, reply and task from the last 14 days and group repeats into recurring tasks
Log hours per recurring task and how often it comes back
Mark each task keep, hand off or drop, using the rule: keep only calls that need the founder's money, taste or name
Name 1 owner and 1 check (what good looks like) for each hand off
Founder confirms the list in a 20 minute call
Move each hand off to the board with a start date and a 2 week review
jobs.output: a hand-off list: recurring tasks, hours a week each, new owner and the check, plus founder hours freed
jobs.next: feeds 23-03 (approval rules) and 23-14 (written steps for each handed task)

watch.metric: founder hours a week on tasks with another named owner possible

jobs.drives: decisions waiting on the founder over 48 hours

jobs.job: Log every decision waiting on the founder for more than 48 hours each Monday, and write an approval rule that lets someone else make the 3 most common kinds
jobs.trigger: every Monday before the team meeting

inputs.need: cards in the waiting on approval column with age in hours
current approval rules and budget caps
the founder's red lines

steps: List every card waiting on the founder and how long it has waited
Group them by kind: ad spend change, discount, refund over a limit, new vendor, creative sign-off
Pick the 3 kinds with the most cards
Draft a rule for each with a cap, for example refunds under $150 the CX lead approves
Founder signs or edits each rule
Write the rules to the decisions shelf and route matching cards to the new approver
jobs.output: 3 written approval rules and a weekly count of decisions waiting over 48 hours
jobs.next: feeds 23-10 (Monday meeting) and 26-05 (decisions logged)

watch.metric: decisions waiting on the founder over 48 hours

jobs.drives: founder hours a week and launch dates held

jobs.job: Build the launch plan 4 weeks out: every task, owner, vendor and date timed back from launch day, with the 5 tasks that block others marked red
jobs.trigger: 4 weeks before every launch, sale or new product drop

inputs.need: launch date, product and offer
stock arrival date and units
vendor lead times: photo shoot, creators, agency, warehouse
launch checklist from the last launch and what went wrong

steps: Copy the last launch checklist and add what was missing last time
Time each task back from launch day using real vendor lead times
Give each task 1 owner and put it on the board
Mark the 5 tasks that block others (stock landed, photos, page live, emails built, ads approved)
Check twice a week: any red task 2 days late goes to the founder
Log the launch outcome and what slipped for next time
jobs.output: a dated launch plan on the board with owners and 5 red blocker tasks
jobs.next: feeds 23-10 (Monday meeting) and 25-12 (look-back after the launch)

watch.metric: launch tasks late against plan

jobs.drives: launch on the planned date with stock, page and ads ready

jobs.job: Count open tickets, follow-ups owed and time to resolution per support agent, plus open and late board cards per person, every Monday, and flag anyone 50 percent above the team median
jobs.trigger: every Monday, and daily during a sale

inputs.need: tickets with agent, first reply, resolved time, reopens and follow-ups owed
order value at stake per open ticket
open and late cards per person
each person's weekly hours

steps: Pull last week's tickets per agent: open, resolved, follow-ups owed, median time to resolution, reopens
Pull open and late board cards per person
Divide each by the person's hours to get load per hour
Flag anyone 50 percent above the team median, and any ticket owed a follow-up for over 48 hours
Lead moves 2 cards or 1 queue off each flagged person
Log the moves and check the flag clears next Monday
jobs.output: a load table per person with red flags, and a list of follow-ups owed with the order value at stake
jobs.next: feeds 23-07 (hiring trigger) and 26-04 (service next to money in the weekly pack)

watch.metric: follow-ups owed over 48 hours, and people above 150 percent of median load

jobs.drives: time to resolution and staff who stay

jobs.job: Forecast tickets and orders for the 5 Black Friday days from last year's peak and this year's plan, and turn them into agent and warehouse hours needed against hours booked
jobs.trigger: 6 weeks before Black Friday and any sale over 2x normal orders

inputs.need: last year's orders and tickets per day around the peak
this year's sale plan and expected order lift
tickets an agent closes per hour, and orders packed per warehouse hour
the 3PL's peak capacity and cut-off times

steps: Pull daily orders and tickets for last year's peak window
Scale by this year's plan to get orders and tickets per day
Divide by closes per agent hour and orders per pack hour
Set hours needed against hours booked per day and name the gap
Book temps or overtime, or add macros and a where is my order page to cut tickets
Check the plan against real volume each peak day
jobs.output: a peak staffing table: 5 days, hours needed, hours booked, the gap, and the fix for each gap
jobs.next: feeds 24-19 (peak readiness check)

watch.metric: staff hours planned against staff hours needed for peak days

jobs.drives: first reply time and ship time held on peak days

jobs.job: Write the hiring trigger per team as a number, like tickets per agent per day or orders per ops person per week, and check it each month against the last 8 weeks
jobs.trigger: once, then monthly, and whenever someone asks to hire

inputs.need: tickets per agent per day, 8 weeks
orders per week
team list with roles and hours
the cost of a hire and the cash floor

steps: Compute load per person per team for the last 8 weeks
Founder sets the trigger per team, for example 80 tickets per agent per day for 4 weeks running
Check the upstream fixes first (23-08) and note what they would cut
Compare this month's load with the trigger and say hire, wait or fix upstream
Log the call and the numbers on the decisions shelf
jobs.output: a hiring trigger per team and a monthly hire, wait or fix call with the numbers behind it
jobs.next: feeds 26-20 (month close)

watch.metric: workload per person against the written hiring trigger

jobs.drives: hires made on time, and payroll as a share of gross profit

jobs.job: Rank ticket types by count per 100 orders and agent minutes, and give the top 3 an owner outside support with an upstream fix like a size chart, a tracking email or an FAQ line
jobs.trigger: monthly, and when tickets per 100 orders rise 20 percent

inputs.need: tickets tagged by type with handle time
orders per week
where each question is answered today
support macros and policies

steps: Tag the last 30 days of tickets by type and count per 100 orders
Multiply by handle time to get agent hours per type
Pick the top 3 types and name the upstream cause for each
Give each fix an owner outside support (site, ops, email) and a date on the board
Check tickets per 100 orders for that type 30 days after the fix
jobs.output: top 3 repeat ticket types with a named fix, owner and date, and the hours each costs a month
jobs.next: feeds 07 (landing page fixes) and 15 (CX help center)

watch.metric: tickets per 100 orders for the top 3 types

jobs.drives: support cost per order

jobs.job: Track each open purchase order through sample, materials, production, quality check and ship against the factory's plan every week, and show what a slip does to launch date and stock
jobs.trigger: every Monday while a purchase order is open, and when the factory goes quiet for 5 days

inputs.need: open purchase orders with units, dates and factory
factory production steps and promised dates
inputs.from: supplier emails or purchase order file

inputs.need: stock on hand and weekly sell rate per product
launch dates tied to the stock

steps: List each open order with its 5 steps and promised dates
Ask the factory for a dated update every Monday and log it
Mark any step late against plan
Compute the new landing date and weeks of stock left at today's sell rate
Say what moves: launch date, ad spend on that product, or air freight for part
Put the call on the board with an owner
jobs.output: a purchase order tracker with late steps in red and the stock-out date each slip causes
jobs.next: feeds 19 (supply and inventory) and 23-04 (launch plan)

watch.metric: production steps late against plan, per open order

jobs.drives: stock-outs avoided and launch dates held

jobs.job: Run the Monday meeting from the board: 6 numbers, the cards waiting on approval, the late cards, and 3 calls to make, ending with an owner and a date for each call
jobs.trigger: every Monday

inputs.need: 6 weekly numbers: sales, gross profit after ads, new customers, cost per new customer, stock days on top sellers, first reply time
inputs.from: store platform, Meta Ads, Google Ads and helpdesk

inputs.need: cards waiting and late
decisions log

steps: Open the 6 numbers and the 3 biggest movers
Walk only the waiting and late cards, not every card
Pick 3 calls and decide each in the room
Give each call 1 owner and a date, and put it on the board
Log the calls to the decisions shelf
Count decisions made; if 0, cut the meeting to 30 minutes next week
jobs.output: 3 logged decisions per week with owner and date, and a meeting that ends on time
jobs.next: feeds 26-05 (decisions logged in the weekly pack)

watch.metric: decisions with an owner and date made in the weekly meeting

jobs.drives: founder hours in meetings and speed of calls

jobs.job: Map every critical login, supplier contact, file and recurring task to the people who can do it today, and mark every one with only 1 person in red
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then every quarter and when anyone gives notice

inputs.need: account list with admins
supplier, 3PL, agency and bank contacts
recurring tasks with current doer
who knows what, from each team member in a 10 minute survey

steps: List critical items: store owner login, Meta Business, payouts, domain, 3PL portal, factory contact, reorder file, payroll file
For each, ask who can do or reach it today
Mark items with 1 person red, 2 people amber, 3 or more green
Name a backup for each red item and a date to train them
Put each backup training on the board
Recount red items next quarter
jobs.output: a single-person risk map with each red item's backup and training date
jobs.next: feeds 23-12 (handover on notice) and 23-13 (cover for a founder break)

watch.metric: critical logins, contacts and tasks only one person can do

jobs.drives: days of disruption when a person leaves

jobs.job: Run a 10 day handover when someone gives notice: list what they hold, record a 5 minute screen video per core task, move each login to a company account, and name the new owner
jobs.trigger: the day someone gives notice

inputs.need: the leaver's tasks, logins and contacts
screen recorder (Loom or the built-in one)
who takes over each part

steps: Pull everything the person holds from the owner map and the access register
Book 3 sessions: tasks, contacts, logins
Record a 5 minute video per core task and file it with the written steps
Move logins and 2-step devices to company accounts
Name the new owner for each item and have them do each task once before day 10
Close the leaver's access on the last day (23-15)
jobs.output: a handover pack: tasks with videos and new owners, logins moved, and contacts introduced
jobs.next: feeds 23-15 (close access on the last day)

watch.metric: items handed over and tested by the new owner before the last day

jobs.drives: no stopped work after a departure

jobs.job: 2 weeks before a founder break, list the founder-only tasks and decisions due in the window, name a cover and a spend cap for each, and write what counts as an emergency
jobs.trigger: 2 weeks before any founder break of 5 days or more

inputs.need: founder's recurring tasks and decisions
calendar for the break window: launches, payouts, renewals
approval rules and caps

steps: List founder tasks and decisions due in the break window
Name a cover for each and a cap they can spend or approve alone
Write the emergency rule: account takeover, payout hold, stock-out on a top seller, press problem
Set alerts so only emergencies reach the founder
Cover runs 1 day of the founder's tasks before the break as a test
jobs.output: a cover plan: each task, its cover, the cap, and a 4 item emergency list
jobs.next: feeds 26-02 (away mode: only flags reach the founder)

watch.metric: founder-only tasks with a named cover

jobs.drives: founder switches off; no stalled decisions in the window

jobs.job: Write step lists for the 10 core recurring tasks, like reorder, returns, daily ad check, payouts and sale setup, and test each by having someone else do it once from the page
jobs.trigger: once, then every 6 months, and before each new hire starts

inputs.need: the 10 core recurring tasks
support macros and policies
screen videos from the current doer

steps: Pick the 10 tasks that stop the business if skipped for a week
Current doer writes the steps in under 1 page with screenshots
Someone else does the task once from the page and marks where they got stuck
Fix the page and date it
Set a review date 6 months out
For a new hire, tick off each task they run alone by week 8
jobs.output: 10 tested step lists with a review date, and a week 8 checklist for new hires
jobs.next: feeds 23-12 (handover) and 23-13 (break cover)

watch.metric: core roles with written steps reviewed in the last 6 months

jobs.drives: weeks until a new hire runs their job alone

jobs.job: When anyone leaves, close or move every account they can reach the same day from the security folder, and log what was closed and when
jobs.trigger: the last working day of any staff member, freelancer or agency

inputs.need: register of accounts and who has access
admin pages on store, Meta, Google, email tool, helpdesk, bank
the leaver's name and end date

steps: Pull every account the person or agency can reach from the register
Remove or downgrade each one, starting with store owner, Meta Business, payouts and domain
Rotate any shared keys or app tokens they held
Log each change with time and who did it
Recheck 7 days later that nothing was re-added
jobs.output: an offboarding log with every account closed on the day, and 0 open accounts for people who left
jobs.next: feeds 24-04 (monthly stale access sweep)

watch.metric: accounts still open for people who left

jobs.drives: no lost data, spend or customers on the way out

jobs.job: Check every order's ship time against the 3PL's contract ship time each week, and daily during a sale, and total the late orders and the credits owed
jobs.trigger: every Monday, and daily when late-order tickets jump

inputs.need: orders with paid time and fulfilled time
contract ship time, cut-off and credit terms
tickets tagged late or where is my order
3PL order export if fulfilled times do not sync

steps: Compute hours from paid to shipped for every order, using the contract's cut-off
Mark each order on time or late and total per day
Match late orders to where is my order tickets
Compute credits owed under the contract
Send the 3PL the list with order numbers and ask for credit and a fix date
Log the claim and check it lands on the next invoice
jobs.output: a weekly ship time table, late orders by day, and a credit claim with order numbers
jobs.next: feeds 23-18 (invoice audit) and 26-04 (service in the weekly pack)

watch.metric: orders shipped within the contract ship time

jobs.drives: late-order tickets and repeat rate of affected buyers

jobs.job: Tag wrong item and damaged tickets by order, compute the error rate per 1,000 orders each week, and send the 3PL the list with the credits owed
jobs.trigger: every Monday

inputs.need: tickets tagged wrong item or damaged, with order number and photo
orders shipped per week
contract error rate and credit terms

steps: Pull wrong item and damaged tickets and link each to its order
Compute errors per 1,000 orders per week, split by product
Compare with the contract's allowed rate
List reship and refund cost per error
Send the 3PL the list and ask for credit and a root cause per product
jobs.output: a weekly pick error rate, errors per product and a credit claim
jobs.next: feeds 23-18 (invoice audit)

watch.metric: wrong or damaged item orders per 1,000

jobs.drives: reship and refund cost, and review rating

jobs.job: Check every line of the monthly 3PL invoice against the contract rates and the store's own order and unit counts in code, and list the lines to dispute
jobs.trigger: when each 3PL invoice arrives

inputs.need: the 3PL invoice as CSV or PDF
contract rate card: pick, pack, storage, postage, extras
orders, units and shipments for the month

steps: Load the invoice lines into a table
Recompute each line from the rate card and the store's own counts in code
Mark lines that do not match, with the dollar gap
Add credits owed from 23-16 and 23-17
Send the dispute list before the payment date
Track the fulfilment cost per order by part month over month
jobs.output: an invoice check: matched lines, disputed lines with dollars, and cost per order by part
jobs.next: feeds 21 (finance and cash) and 23-19 (vendor renewal)

watch.metric: invoice lines that do not match contract rates or order counts

jobs.drives: fulfilment cost per order

jobs.job: Score the agency each month on deliverables due against delivered and late, and on contribution margin from its channel after its fee, and bring the scorecard to every renewal call
jobs.trigger: monthly, and 30 days before the retainer renews

inputs.need: the scope: deliverables per month
agency deliverables with due and delivered dates
ad spend and store orders from the agency's channel
inputs.from: Meta Ads, Google Ads and store platform

inputs.need: product cost, shipping and fees

steps: List deliverables due this month from the scope
Mark each delivered on time, late or missed from board dates
Compute contribution margin from the channel after ad spend and the agency fee
Show 3 months side by side
Write the call: renew, renegotiate with named fixes, or leave
jobs.output: an agency scorecard: on time share, missed items, and profit after fee for 3 months
jobs.next: feeds 26-18 (invoice check against delivered work)

watch.metric: agency deliverables late or missed against the scope

jobs.drives: contribution margin from the agency's channel after its fee

jobs.job: List every software charge on the card with its monthly cost, owner and last login, and cancel tools unused in 60 days before their renewal date
jobs.trigger: once, then monthly, and 30 days before any annual renewal

inputs.need: card and bank statements for 3 months
installed store apps with cost
last login per tool from each admin page
apps and stack with owner

steps: Pull every recurring charge from 3 months of statements
Match each to a tool, an owner and what it does
Check last login or usage for each
Mark cancel, keep or downgrade, and list renewal dates in the next 60 days
Owner confirms, then cancel and log the monthly saving
jobs.output: a software list with cost, owner, last use and renewal date, plus a cancel list and the saving
jobs.next: feeds 08-site-speed app audit and 21 (finance and cash)

watch.metric: monthly software cost for tools unused in 60 days

jobs.drives: operating cost as a share of revenue

new_enablers.name: Owner and backup map
new_enablers.what: A register of every recurring task, critical login, supplier contact and key file, with its 1 owner, its backup, its written steps and a review date. Marks anything only 1 person can do.

new_enablers.name: Vendor scorecard
new_enablers.what: Holds each vendor's contract terms (ship time, error rate, rates, deliverables) and checks them each week or month against the store's own orders, tickets and invoices. Totals misses and credits owed.

new_enablers.name: Team load and capacity plan
new_enablers.what: Joins tickets per agent, orders per ops person, open and late cards per person and hours booked, against a written hiring trigger. Forecasts hours needed for peak days from last year's peak and this year's plan.
